text:
Jess M: Heads-up — we got a support ticket where a Dedicated customer hit a sustained spike and their requests silently fell back to hosted. They only noticed when cost spiked and latency changed.

Omar R: Ugh. Do we have metric surfaces that show "spillover" in the console today? I thought we emitted something but probably not customer-facing.

Kai L: We emit internal events (routing.fallback) but nothing in the tenant dashboard. That was deliberate for isolation concerns.

Jess M: The customer wants visibility and a per-route history so they can adjust autoscale or raise their committed capacity. Not seeing it in the console means they keep chasing blame.

Anika P: UX ask: show a lightweight timeline per-route: #requests, %served_by_dedicated, %served_by_hosted, and a short "why" (e.g., capacity saturating, model mismatch). Keep it off by default for compliance-sensitive tenants.

Omar R: We also need to decide billing semantics. If tenant is billed reserved-rate but spillovers hit hosted, do we charge hosted rate or keep committed price? current behavior: hosted charged (so customer complained).

Kai L: From an isolation standpoint, we can't promise dedicated-level SLA if we allow spillover. We should surface a clear policy and a per-tenant flag: allow_spillover: true/false. If false, requests queue or 429.

Jess M: Agreed. Proposal: default for enterprise Dedicated is allow_spillover=false, but offer an opt-in policy that does allow spillover and explicitly shows in console (and invoice) when it happens.

Omar R: To implement we need three pieces: 1) telemetry (metrics + traces) 2) API/response headers for debugging 3) console UI for history and billing mapping.

Kai L: Telemetry names proposal: routes.spillover.count, routes.spillover.latency_p50/p95, routes.fallback.model_id, tenant.routing_policy.allow_spillover. Add a tag served_by={dedicated,hosted,variant:<model>} on each request trace.

Anika P: For the UX: show an on-demand dropdown "Show fallback history" with a small modal explaining: "Requests may be routed to hosted when dedicated capacity is full or model variant incompatible." Link to docs + link to billing line items.

Jess M: Does anyone object to returning a short header to callers for debugging? e.g. "X-Redwood-Served-By: dedicated:v2 | hosted:open-7b"

Kai L: I'm meh — leaking that to product code could encourage customers to build brittle logic around routing. But it's useful for debugging. Maybe make it available behind a debug query param or developer key.

Omar R: Implementation sketch (routing config snippet):
```yaml
route: /generate
model_preference: [redwood-dedicated:v2, redwood-hosted:compat-7b]
fallback_policy: allow_hosted_if_dedicated_full
allow_spillover: true
```

Omar R: And add a flag: expose_served_by_header: false|true|debug-only in tenant profile.

Anika P: For billing: attach a spillover attribution tag to the call so invoice lines can include both reserved consumption and hosted overage. This needs product + finance alignment.

Jess M: One more internal API debate: should the routing decision be synchronous (route at front door) or async (accept->attempt dedicated->if stall then retry on hosted)? Current runtime does quick handshake with pool manager. If we sync, latency penalty might be minimal but complexity higher.

Kai L: We should avoid extra tail latency. My preference: attempt dedicated with a short, configurable deadline (e.g., 100ms). If no token, fall back to hosted. Configurable per-tenant.

Omar R: That deadline should be surfaced in metrics and console so ops can tune. Also add an observable "fallback_reason" enum (capacity, model_incompatible, region_unavailable, maintenance).

Anika P: Draft console label ideas: "Fallbacks this week: 12 (capacity: 9, region: 2, maintenance: 1) — Click to view timeline". Also callout badge during rollouts: "Current model variant uses hosted fallback — expected behavior?" :warning:

Jess M: I'll open an RFC capturing: telemetry schema, routing config flags, header policy, and billing attribution. Want a quick POC for metrics + header behind a tenant flag. Omar/Kai can you pair on the backend? Anika can prototype the modal copy.

Omar R: Yes, I'll take the POC for the header + metrics. Will add the metric names Kai suggested.

Kai L: I'll audit the runtime path to ensure we can implement the 100ms handoff and tag traces appropriately.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/serve-debug-header -> staging (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

Jess M: Nice. Let's keep the default behavior conservative for Dedicated customers, and only enable spillover with explicit consent and clear console visibility.

Anika P: Also update docs + FAQ: "What happens when Dedicated is full?" with clear examples and billing callouts.

Jess M: Thanks all — I'll drop the RFC link here when created.

Omar R: thx — will push a tiny telemetry PR today so we have a first data point.
